resetBook.title: Reset book data
resetBook.description: Deletes the synced transactions and journals of {{book}}; the next sync rebuilds them. Your decisions and documents are kept: reviews, pairs, custody components, loan marks, source-of-funds links, attachments, notes, tags and price edits. They attach again when their transactions come back; anything that no longer matches is held for review. Wallet and backend connections stay, and so does the shared fiat-rate cache unless you clear it below.
resetBook.passphraseHint: Enter the database passphrase and the book name to continue.
resetBook.plaintextHint: These books are not encrypted, so type the confirmation word and the book name to continue.
resetBook.clearRatesHint: Shared by every book in this data folder. Leave it off to keep the BTC-EUR and BTC-USD rate history.
resetBook.wipeHint: Also deletes this book's decisions and documents, including attachment files and anything kept from an earlier reset. Only wallet and backend connections remain; nothing comes back with the next sync.
resetBook.notifyBody: Cleared {{summary}}. Wallet and backend connections were kept.
resetBook.notifyKeptBody: Deleted {{transactions}} transactions and {{journalRows}} journal rows. Kept {{decisions}} decisions; sync the book's wallets to bind them again.

deleteBooks.errorGeneric: Could not delete the book set.

touchIdEnroll.notifyBody: Your passphrase is saved in the macOS Keychain for Touch ID.

touchId.removeFailedBody: macOS Keychain did not remove the saved passphrase.

touchId.forgetAllBody: Touch ID and the CLI's saved unlock were removed for these books.
touchId.forgetAllConfirm: Remove every saved unlock method for these books? You will need the database passphrase next time.
touchId.forgetAllCredentialWarning: The system keychain did not confirm that every saved entry was removed.

marketData.rebuildingFootnote: Fetching missing rates. The count updates when journals finish.

marketData.krakenPathAria: Kraken CSV, ZIP, or folder path
marketData.filePickerUnavailable: Use the path field in browser mode
marketData.bundledDescription: BTC-EUR and BTC-USD hourly rates back to 2011, shipped with Kassiber. Before Kraken's own history they are derived from daily rates. Nothing is downloaded.
marketData.pickArchiveTitle: Choose Kraken OHLCVT CSV or ZIP
marketData.pickUpdateTitle: Choose Kraken update OHLCVT CSV or ZIP
marketData.importPathError: Enter a local Kraken CSV or ZIP path.

marketData.autoDisabledBody: This book uses built-in and imported rates only and contacts no rate provider.

coarse.reviewToggleDescription: On: transactions priced only from a daily rate wait in quarantine until you confirm them or fetch an exact price. Off (default): they are booked at the daily rate and flagged.

bitcoinRails.toggleDescription: On (default): moves between your own BTC and L-BTC are suggested as carrying value, not a sale. Off: they are suggested as taxable. A choice you make on a pair always wins.

privacy.offlineOn: Nothing leaves this device: no wallet sync, rates, update checks or remote AI. Local AI providers keep working.
privacy.offlineOff: Kassiber connects only to services you set up, and only when a task needs them.
privacy.offlineEnvironment: An environment variable (KASSIBER_NO_EGRESS) already blocks wallet and backend connections. Turn on offline mode to also block AI providers and update checks.
privacy.offlineFailed: Could not change offline mode. Try again.
privacy.clipboardOn: Copied addresses and other values are cleared from the clipboard after 30 seconds.
privacy.clipboardOff: Copied values stay in the clipboard until replaced.
privacy.notificationsOn: While Kassiber is in the background, finished work or something that needs you shows a generic system notification.
privacy.notificationsOff: Background work is reported only inside the app.
privacy.notificationsDisclosure: A notification only ever says “Background work needs your attention.”, “Background work has finished.” or “New activity in Kassiber.”, never amounts, counts, book or wallet names, addresses or error details. Your system may still keep notifications and show them on the lock screen, and they reveal that you use Kassiber.
privacy.updatesOn: Kassiber may check GitHub once a day after startup, and whenever you ask from the menu or CLI. GitHub sees your IP address, exact Kassiber version and the time; no book or wallet data is sent.
privacy.updatesOff: Nothing contacts GitHub, including Check for Updates… and the CLI.
privacy.updatesSaveFailedBody: The previous setting is still in effect.
privacy.updatesTrust: Update notices are not signed yet; Kassiber relies on HTTPS and the project's GitHub repository. You always download updates yourself.
privacy.leavesDescription: Every service Kassiber is set up to contact, grouped by what it can see.
privacy.thirdPartyWarning: {{count}} third-party services can see your queries. Mark servers you run as yours, or use Tor.
privacy.thirdPartyWarning_one: {{count}} third-party service can see your queries. Mark servers you run as yours, or use Tor.
privacy.noThirdPartyWithAi: No third-party service sees your queries. Assistant providers are listed below.
privacy.noThirdParty: No third-party service sees your queries.
privacy.filterAllHint: Every service Kassiber is set up to contact.
privacy.assistantEnabled: Local providers keep prompts on this device. Remote providers and subscription apps see your prompts, which can include book data.
privacy.assistantDisabled: The assistant is off, so nothing is sent. Provider settings stay saved.
privacy.modeNormal: Amounts, addresses and percentages are shown.
privacy.modeHideAmounts: Balances, addresses and amounts are hidden until you reveal them.
privacy.modeHideAll: Also hides percentages and shares of your holdings.
privacy.unlockOn: Every launch and unlock starts with amounts hidden.
privacy.clipboardContained: Copies stay on this device and are marked so clipboard-history apps skip them.
privacy.screenShareLabel: Hide amounts while the screen is shared
privacy.screenShareOn: While your screen is shared or recorded, amounts are hidden. Your previous choice returns when it ends.
privacy.screenShareOff: Amounts stay as you set them while the screen is shared or recorded.
privacy.screenShareUnavailable: This system does not tell apps when the screen is shared. Hide amounts yourself before you share.
privacy.screenShareActive: Screen sharing or recording detected. Amounts are hidden until it ends.
privacy.screenShareToastBody: Your screen is being shared or recorded. Amounts come back when it ends.
privacy.explorerFallbacksOn: Without an explorer of your own, transaction and address links open on a public website, which learns what you look up.
privacy.explorerFallbacksOff: Links open only on an explorer you added; without one, no links are shown.
privacy.explorerFallbacksUnavailable: Manual and regtest setups never open public explorer websites.

data.importDescription: Exchange CSVs, wallet history and BIP-329 labels.
data.databaseSizeWal: Plus {{size}} of recent changes not yet merged into the file.
data.osBackupLabel: Keep unencrypted books out of Time Machine
data.osBackupExcluded: This book is not encrypted, so Time Machine skips its database and the attachments and exports Kassiber keeps for it. Keep a copy with an encrypted backup, or encrypt the book.
data.osBackupEncrypted: This book is encrypted, so Time Machine backs it up as encrypted data. Its attachments and exports are plain files and are backed up as they are.
data.osBackupOff: Time Machine backs up this book as it is stored on disk.
data.osBackupFailed: Some of this book's files could not be marked for Time Machine to skip.
data.osBackupOther: Your system's backup tool decides what it saves. Exclude this book's folder there, or encrypt the book.
data.syncedFolderWarning: This unencrypted book is in a folder {{service}} syncs, so its database leaves this device in plain text. Move the book to a local folder or encrypt it.
data.resetWelcomeDescription: Returns to the Welcome screen. Your books are not touched.
data.resetBookDescription: Deletes synced transactions and journals, which the next sync rebuilds. Your decisions, documents and connections are kept.
data.deleteBooksDescription: Deletes this book set and its books from the local database.
data.resetRegtestDescription: Destroy the local regtest Bitcoin node and its chain, then rebuild the full demo book from scratch. Development only; takes a few minutes.
data.resetRegtestConfirm: This deletes the regtest chain and the demo book, then rebuilds both from scratch. It runs the Docker regtest node and takes a few minutes. Continue?
data.resetRegtestDoneBody: A fresh regtest chain and demo book are ready.
data.resetRegtestErrorBody: The regtest environment could not be rebuilt. Check that Docker is running.

ai.featuresDescription: Ask about your books in the side panel and on the Assistant page. Turning it off keeps your settings.
ai.agentsDescription: Claude Code, Codex and other MCP agents can use this book. What they read goes to their AI provider.
ai.agentsError: Could not change external agent access.
ai.agentsGrantReadHint: Agents can read this book. They change nothing and contact no service.
ai.agentsGrantOperatorHint: Agents can also process journals, export, record source-of-funds evidence and documents, and sync wallets and rates, which contacts your configured backends and rate sources.
ai.agentsGrantDecisionsHint: Agents can also make accounting decisions: resolve quarantine, pair or dismiss transfers, record custody, loan and source-of-funds decisions, and edit notes, tags, exclusions and classifications.
ai.agentsRestrictHint: Redacted results only: no transaction IDs, outpoints or labels, and no custody-gap, lineage or chain-analysis source tools. Descriptors, xpubs, secrets and file paths are never sent either way.
ai.agentsAdminNever: Admin work (secrets, backups, deletions, passphrases) is never available to agents.
ai.agentsHostApproval: Your agent's own tool approval is the only prompt before a change. Admin work (secrets, backups, deletions, passphrases) is never available to agents. A running agent may need a restart to show changed tools.
ai.agentsSessionLocked: This book is encrypted. Agents can use it only while you unlock it for them.
ai.agentsSessionActive: Agents you allow can use this book until you lock Kassiber, after {{minutes}} minutes without calls, or after 8 hours at most.
ai.agentsSessionExisting: Already unlocked for agents in a terminal.
ai.agentsSessionError: Could not change agent access to this book.
ai.agentsSessionWaiting: Start your agent; it appears here for you to allow.
ai.checkPrivacy: Nothing is contacted until you press Check, and off-device providers ask first.
ai.checkHint: Ask {{name}} now whether it is installed, signed in and reachable.
ai.checkConfirm_one: Check {{names}} now? Kassiber starts its CLI or contacts its endpoint, which may reach the provider's service. Prompts are not sent.
ai.checkConfirm_other: Check {{names}} now? Kassiber starts their CLIs or contacts their endpoints, which may reach the providers' services. Prompts are not sent.
ai.apiFormatTitle: API format the next chat speaks
ai.restrictedAccessNote: Restricted: the assistant gets redacted results and no custody-gap, lineage or source-acquisition tools.
ai.omitStoreNote: Sends requests without Kassiber's no-retention flag (store: false); the provider's own retention applies.
ai.defaultCannotDisable: The default provider stays on. Set another default first.
ai.deleteConfirm: Delete AI provider '{{name}}'? Cannot be undone.
ai.signInCli: Uses the CLI's own login; Kassiber never reads or stores it.
ai.fastModeNote: Fast mode is available for some models. It is billed at a higher rate, so it is chosen per chat in the model picker and never saved as a default.

status.stale: The last check failed; showing the earlier result.
status.offline: Offline mode is on. Only local providers can be checked.
status.aiOff: Turn on the assistant to check providers.
status.switchedOff: Off. Turn it on to check it.

mode.auto: Store chats only while the database is encrypted.
mode.on: Always store chats, even on an unencrypted database.

chatHistory.description: Kept inside the database, never as files, and left out of diagnostics and audit exports.
chatHistory.effectiveEncrypted: Chats are currently stored inside the encrypted database.
chatHistory.effectiveOnUnencrypted: Chats are currently stored inside the unencrypted database because history is set to on.
chatHistory.effectiveNotStoredAuto: Chats are not stored because the database is not encrypted. Encrypting it turns history on.

developer.intro: Features still being built stay out of the way until you turn them on. Your choice is kept across updates.
developer.enableOn: Early-stage pages are visible in the side nav, in Settings, and in search.
developer.enableOff: Early-stage pages are hidden or greyed out.
developer.alphaBannerDescription: The red Alpha label in the title bar. Hiding it doesn't make Kassiber any less alpha.
developer.bufferDescription: Logs stay in memory on this device: {{retained}} now, at most {{records}} records or {{bytes}}. Closing or refreshing the app clears them unless you export them first.

kindHint.local: Runs on this machine. No data leaves the device.
kindHint.remote: Cloud, LAN, or vendor CLI provider. Prompts may leave the device.
kindHint.tee: Provider claims a trusted-execution / attestation path (e.g. Maple AI). Kassiber still treats it as off-device.
kindHint.cli_proxy: A CLI proxy passes prompts on to the services behind your subscriptions, so it is always treated as off this device. Each model is spoken in the format its family needs.

presetHint.ollama: Runs models on this device. Start it with:
presetHint.lmstudio: Start the server in LM Studio's Developer tab, or with:
presetHint.vllm: The assistant needs tools, which vLLM offers only with a tool parser for your model (hermes suits Qwen). Start it with:
presetHint.llamacpp: The assistant needs tools, which llama.cpp offers only with --jinja. Start it with:
presetHint.omlx: Runs models on this Mac with Apple silicon. Start it from its menu-bar app, or with:

presetHint.cliProxy: A CLIProxyAPI server that serves the subscriptions you are signed in to (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, …) as one API. Enter its address and, if it has one, its client key; Test & discover lists its models.

autoRemote.url: This address isn't on this device, so it's treated as remote.
autoRemote.cli: CLI agents can send prompts off this device, so this provider is treated as remote.

aiProvider.keyClearedForAddress: API key cleared because the address changed.
aiProvider.exemptionResetForAddress: No-retention exemption reset for the new address.
aiProvider.formatResetForAddress: API format reset to Auto for the new address.

aiProvider.restrictAccessLabel: Restrict what the assistant can use
aiProvider.restrictAccessHint: Off by default: the assistant can use every tool and gets full results, including custody gaps and lineage, chain-analysis sources and an attachment's cell values. Restricted keeps this provider to redacted results. Descriptors, xpubs, secrets and file paths are never sent either way.
aiProvider.omitStoreLabel: Send requests without Kassiber's no-retention flag
aiProvider.omitStoreHint: Only for an endpoint that refuses store: false. Chat Completions requests then go without it, and the provider's own retention applies to your prompts and tool results.
aiProvider.remoteWarning: Prompts may leave this device. CLI agents (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot) use your local CLI authentication/config and can forward Kassiber context to external model services. Do not paste raw credentials, wallet exports, or private descriptors unless your threat model allows it.
aiProvider.remoteAck: I understand prompts and selected Kassiber context may leave this device through this provider.
aiProvider.testOkBinary: CLI found — model availability and authentication are checked when chat starts.
aiProvider.testToolsRefused: This endpoint answered but refused tools, so the assistant can't read your book through it.
aiProvider.testStoreRefused: This endpoint refuses Kassiber's no-retention flag (store: false), so chats with it will fail. Under Advanced you can send requests without the flag; the provider's own retention then applies.
aiProvider.testStoreOmitted: Sent without Kassiber's no-retention flag; the provider's own retention applies.
aiProvider.testNoReply_one: Connected — {{count}} model listed, but no reply was checked.
aiProvider.testNoReply_other: Connected — {{count}} models listed, but no reply was checked.
aiProvider.testNoModel: Choose a model to check that it can answer.

aiProvider.errorSaveBeforeTest: Save the provider before testing a new API key.
aiProvider.errorTestDisabled: This provider is disabled. Turn it on in Settings → Assistant to test it.
aiProvider.errorCliLocalPosture: CLI agents (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot) may send prompts off-device. Choose remote or TEE.
aiProvider.errorAckRequired: Acknowledge that prompts may leave this device before saving.
aiProvider.errorAckRequiredTest: Testing sends a short prompt to this provider. Acknowledge that prompts may leave this device first.

backendModal.backendSourceHint: A public server from the list, or one you run.
backendModal.presetEndpointHint: The operators listed here state that they keep no logs.
backendModal.endpointTypeHint: What your server speaks: an Explorer API (Esplora) over HTTP, or Electrum / Fulcrum over TCP/SSL.

backendModal.silentPaymentsHint: Only for a local scanner or a backend that states it supports Silent Payments.
backendModal.silentPaymentsScannerConfigHint: Set a scanner file on this device, or a scan path on this backend. Saved paths stay hidden; leave a field blank to keep it.

certificateTrust.title: Server certificate
certificateTrust.description: Check the TLS certificate {{backend}} presents and decide whether to trust it.
certificateTrust.introBody: Kassiber will connect to this server once to read its certificate. Nothing is trusted until you compare the fingerprint and confirm it.
certificateTrust.untrustedNotice: This server's certificate is not signed by an authority Kassiber trusts. That is normal for your own node with a self-signed certificate.
certificateTrust.changedWarning: This server's certificate changed. Kassiber will not accept the new certificate on its own. If you did not replace the certificate on your server yourself, someone may be impersonating it: do not trust it.
certificateTrust.subject: Issued to
certificateTrust.compare: Compare this fingerprint with the one your server shows. Trust it only if they match exactly.
certificateTrust.replaces: Trusting this replaces the certificate trusted before (its fingerprint is shown above as previously trusted).
certificateTrust.clearsInsecure: Trusting it also turns certificate verification back on for this backend.
certificateTrust.trusted: Certificate trusted. Kassiber now accepts only this certificate from {{host}}.
certificateTrust.rowHint: For your own server with a self-signed certificate: see its fingerprint and trust it once.
certificateTrust.saveFirst: Save the backend first, then check its certificate.
certificateTrust.testUntrusted: The server's certificate is not trusted yet.
certificateTrust.testChanged: The server's certificate changed since you trusted it.

errors.alreadyTrusted: This server's certificate is already trusted. There is nothing to confirm.
errors.unpinnable: This certificate cannot be trusted: it is expired, not yet valid, or not an ordinary TLS server certificate.
errors.plaintext: This backend does not use TLS, so there is no certificate to trust.
errors.unsupported: Certificate trust is not available for this kind of backend.
errors.mismatch: The server now presents a different certificate than the one you saw. Nothing was trusted; fetch it again and compare.
errors.offline: Kassiber is in offline mode. Turn it off to reach the server.
errors.connection: Could not reach the server to read its certificate.
errors.writeFailed: The certificate could not be saved in the book's data folder.
errors.changedSinceReview: This backend's address, proxy or certificate settings changed after you fetched the certificate. Nothing was trusted; fetch it again.
errors.overridden: Environment variables override this backend's connection settings, so a trusted certificate might not be used. Nothing was trusted.

trust.onDeviceNote: Runs on this device or your local network; queries stay inside your network.
trust.selfNote: A server you run. Queries leave this device but only reach your own server.
trust.torNote: Reached over Tor: the server sees your queries, but not your IP address.
trust.proxyNote: Only this backend goes through its proxy: the server sees your queries, but not your IP address.
trust.remoteNote: Someone else runs this server and sees your queries. Use your own server or a proxy to avoid that.
